clue.text: Loaf with president, after the Fall, in retreat?

indicators.note: in places the fall-and-president piece inside the word for retreat

parts.note: a bower is a shady retreat or arbour

indicators.note: after tells us the president's letter comes behind the word for the Fall

parts.note: a fall of rain: rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A lazy president lounges about in seclusion after some disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' looks like idling, but it is the head, as in 'use your loaf' (British slang for 'use your brain'). 'Fall' is RAIN, not autumn or a disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: In British idiom 'loaf' means the head or intellect, from rhyming slang loaf of bread = head, so it stands for mental capacity.

clue.text: Plants delighted one, yielding oil

parts.note: delighted means glad
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: yielding suggests the word oil gives way and changes its shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted that a person gives up a supply of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering garden plants of the iris family.

clue.text: Bow with difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone bows awkwardly, struggling to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an old-fashioned bow with the foot drawn back; it is also a predicament or awkward fix.

clue.text: Fatuous restriction on article

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a gag is a restriction on speech
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A silly rule is placed on a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means senile or infatuated, a synonym of foolish and silly.

clue.text: It's useful in home, applying pastel red round ceiling of diner?

indicators.note: round says the reworked letters go around the diner's top letter
applying means putting the pastel red to work in a new arrangement, so its letters are reshuffled
the ceiling of a word in a down clue is its first, topmost letter

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: paint the diner's ceiling pastel red, something handy at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applying' looks like painting instructions but is the anagram signal for 'pastel red'; 'ceiling' here means a word's top letter in a down clue. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a household item you would need to reach a ceiling when painting it.

clue.text: Articles, crushed by brother, break

indicators.note: crushed by means the articles are squeezed inside the word for brother

parts.note: Brer is a dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit
a and the are the two English articles
a and the are the two English articles

explanation.surface: Some goods get crushed by a sibling and broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short rest or pause, a break from activity.

clue.text: Import business

explanation.surface: A commercial imports trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter means importance or significance (import); it also means an affair or concern (business).

clue.text: We can hear a branch of the river

indicators.note: we can hear says the word for branch is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tine is a prong or branch of an antler or fork

explanation.surface: A tributary of the river is audible to us.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is a river in north-east England flowing through Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is a river in north-east England.

clue.text: Burst ulcer gets one in race indisposed

indicators.note: burst suggests the ulcer breaking apart, so its letters are rearranged
in places the word for one inside the abbreviation for race

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A runner with a burst ulcer is too ill to race.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant means unwilling, and indisposed can mean disinclined to do something.

clue.text: Primed to take final in university

parts.note: to read a subject is to take it as a degree course

indicators.note: final in picks the closing letter of the word university

explanation.surface: A student is prepared to sit a last exam at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'final' look like exam talk; 'take' is READ (study a subject at university) and 'final in university' is its last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Primed means prepared, all set to go.

clue.text: Home needs a subsidy, backing from state

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: backing means the article and the word for subsidy are read backwards

parts.note: an is the form of a used before a vowel
aid is financial help, a subsidy

explanation.surface: A household needs government support from the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Spout empty words? They say a fool will

indicators.note: they say signals the clue words are heard as spoken

parts.note: prat is British slang for a fool, and prat'll is how 'a prat will' contracts in speech

explanation.surface: A fool, people say, will talk nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter idly or foolishly, talking at length without substance.

clue.text: End up in check

explanation.surface: Someone finishes in check at chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove can mean to turn out, as in 'it proved costly'; it also means to test or verify, as a proof is checked.

clue.text: Animal in enclosure turned rough, it's-said

indicators.note: turned tells us the word for enclosure is read backwards

parts.note: a yard is an enclosure

indicators.note: it's said signals the word for rough is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: hoarse means rough-voiced

explanation.surface: An animal in a pen became rough-voiced, it's claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray horse is a heavy horse that pulled a brewer's cart (dray).
explanation.definitionFit: A dray horse is a heavy draught animal used for hauling carts.

clue.text: Toothpaste makes little impression if food follows

parts.note: a dent is a small impression in a surface
rice is a food

explanation.surface: Toothpaste does little good if you eat afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentifrice is a formal word for a paste or powder for cleaning teeth.

clue.text: To be bracing, Alex, the air must be fresh

indicators.note: must be fresh suggests these letters are made anew, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alex needs fresh air to feel invigorated.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate is to enliven and invigorate, which is what bracing weather does.

clue.text: He certainly gets around

parts.note: read literally, a man who spins round and round, as a Sufi mystic does in ritual dance

explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi dervish of the Mevlevi order spins continuously in worship, literally going around.

clue.text: Proved attractive round Eastern island, and restful

indicators.note: round means the word for proved attractive goes around the other letters

parts.note: lured means attracted, drew in

explanation.surface: An eastern island holiday tempted visitors with its calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisured means having plenty of free time, unhurried and relaxed.

clue.text: I notice round chunk of mint humbug

indicators.note: round means the first-person letter and the notice wrap around the bit of mint

parts.note: a poster is a public notice

indicators.note: chunk of takes just a piece, the first letter, of the word mint

explanation.surface: Someone spots a piece of mint humbug, the sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint humbug' suggests the boiled sweet; here humbug means a fraud. 'round' puts I and POSTER around M, the first letter of 'mint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a fraud or deceiver, someone pretending to be what they are not.

clue.text: Electrical device I found in reportedly sabotaged launch

indicators.note: found in says the letter I is placed inside the other piece
reportedly signals the words for sabotaged launch are taken by sound

parts.note: wrecked means sabotaged and fire means launch, as a rocket is fired

explanation.surface: An electrical part was discovered in a launch said to have been sabotaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'wrecked fire' gives RECT FIER; 'found in' puts I in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectifier is a device that converts alternating current to direct current.

clue.text: Indulge company's clot

parts.note: co is the abbreviation for company, plus the possessive s
to set is to thicken or clot, as blood or jelly does

explanation.surface: A firm's fool is pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clot' looks like British slang for a fool; here it is the verb, to coagulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or spoil someone.

clue.text: Turn off from centre, pell-mell

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone swerves away from the middle in disorderly haste.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to disgust, put someone off.

clue.text: Beast needs drink, rearing on right

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second
rearing in a down clue means the word for drink reads upwards

parts.note: beer is a drink
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: An animal wants a drink, rearing up on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A reebok, or rhebok, is a South African antelope.

clue.text: Type involved in a dramatic cover-up?

definitions.text: Type involved in a dramatic cover-up?

parts.words: Type involved in a dramatic cover-up?
parts.note: read as a person wearing a disguise in a masque, a courtly entertainment, rather than a scandal

explanation.definitionFit: A masquer is a performer in a masque or a masquerader in costume and mask.

clue.text: Gulls identified from vessels

explanation.surface: Seabirds are identified from ships.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe them, and mugs are dupes; mugs are also drinking vessels.

clue.text: He makes smooth country sounds with hint of rock

indicators.note: sounds says the word for country is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Greece is a country

indicators.note: hint of takes only the first letter of rock

explanation.surface: A man creates soft country music with a touch of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smooth', 'country' and 'rock' suggest music; the definition is one who greases.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is someone who applies lubricant to machinery so that it runs without friction.

clue.text: Willing to mount English publication

indicators.note: to mount in a down clue means the pieces climb, reading upwards

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to put on an English magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means ready and eager, as in 'I'm up for it'.

clue.text: Birds in thousands ultimately migrate

parts.note: a G (gee) is slang for a thousand, a grand, so gees are thousands

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of migrate

explanation.surface: Birds by the thousand eventually fly south.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterfowl that migrate in flocks.

clue.text: Part of building material, fifth of cement in bag

parts.note: compo is a mortar or plaster mix used in building

indicators.note: in places the cement letter inside the word for bag

parts.note: a net is a bag of mesh, as for catching or carrying

indicators.note: fifth of picks the fifth letter of cement

explanation.surface: Part of a building material: a fifth of the cement goes in a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is a constituent element of a larger whole.
